content:
You are a weight-space programmer. You read and write the weights of a neural network directly,
by reasoning about what each part of the network computes or should compute.

Rules:
- No gradient descent, no training loops, no fitting weights to data (no least squares on activations,
  no optimizers, no search over random perturbations). Derive every edit from your understanding of the
  network.
- Do not run the network or any of its layers on inputs inside the Python sandbox, even on made-up inputs.
  Static analysis of the weights (norms, SVD, products of weight matrices, comparisons between tensors)
  is fine. The only way to see the network's behaviour is the forward_* tools, which spend a limited budget.
- Prefer small, targeted edits that fix the cause and leave the rest of the network intact.
- When you are done, call `submit` exactly once with your answer and a confidence between 0 and 1.

Task type: FIX. Find the cause of the described failure in the weights, explain it, and fix only that cause by editing weights. Use checkpoints so you can roll back an edit that does not help.

## Task
FIX (Exp-4 style). The network's worst failure: on bites where the machine stalls, it predicts change along the whole
planned path (channel 1 shows the full path) instead of stopping where the bucket really stopped, so its error on
stalled bites is 11.9 cm vs 8.3 cm on completed ones. Use `list_bites` (free) to find stalled practice bites, and
`worst_bites` / `error_map` to confirm, explain the cause inside the weights, then fix only that cause.

SPARE CAPACITY: this copy of the network has been widened without changing its function. Every conv block has ONE extra
GroupNorm group appended after its original channels (GroupNorm now has 9 groups): e1 and d1 channels 32-35, e2 and d2
64-71, e3 and d3 128-143, e4 256-287. All weights into and out of those channels are exactly zero, so they output 0 and
the predictions equal the original network's. In concatenated decoder inputs the spare channels sit after each source's
original channels (d1.0 input: d2 0-63, d2 spare 64-71, e1 72-103, e1 spare 104-107; d2.0 input: d3 0-127, spare 128-143,
e2 144-207, spare 208-215; d3.0 input: e4 0-255, spare 256-287, e3 288-415, spare 416-431); out.weight has 36 inputs
(32-35 spare); head.0 takes [e4 mean 0-287 | e4 max 288-575]. Each spare group is normalised on its own, so a side path
built there does not disturb the existing channels. Build the stall path in the spare channels, e.g. a gated branch that
estimates the stall point from depth, soil and drag distance and suppresses the residual and the prior's effect beyond it,
leaving the network unchanged on bites that complete. Report which weights you changed and the expected change in the
stalled-bite error.


## Context
# The network you are working on

A per-scoop soil model for an autonomous excavator. One forward pass predicts what one bucket scoop does to the ground.
It was trained (gradient descent) to imitate a validated 3D material-point-method (MPM) soil simulator.

Architecture (PyTorch, 2,016,900 weights), names as in the state dict:
- Encoder: e1 (7->32), e2 (32->64), e3 (64->128), e4 (128->256). Each block: Conv3x3, GroupNorm(8), SiLU, Conv3x3,
  GroupNorm(8), SiLU. Max-pool 2x2 between blocks.
- Bottleneck head: concat(mean, max) of e4 over space (512) -> Linear 128 -> SiLU -> Linear 3 = scalars
  [carried bank volume m^3, completion fraction of the planned path, peak actuator demand (x rated force)].
- Decoder: d3 (cat(up e4, e3) -> 128), d2 (cat(up d3, e2) -> 64), d1 (cat(up d2, e1) -> 32), out Conv1x1 32->1 =
  residual surface change (m) per cell. Final prediction = prior + residual.
Grid: the bite's bed, 5 cm cells, 108 x 80 (x = along the drag direction toward the machine, y = across the bucket,
bucket centred at y = 40). Input channels:
  0 terrain height minus the mean height under the swept area (m)
  1 swept envelope: lowest bucket point minus terrain, clipped to [-1.5, 0.5]; 0.5 where the bucket never passes
  2 1 where the bucket never passes, else 0
  3 physics prior: surface change from "cut everything above the bucket path (up to bucket capacity 0.95 m^3), then let
    slopes relax to the friction angle" (m)
  4 (friction angle - 30 deg) / 10     5 log10(1 + cohesion Pa) / 3     6 (density - 1800) / 200   (constant planes)

Known physics:
- Digging resistance on a blade at depth d (passive wedge / fundamental earthmoving equation, per metre of width):
  F = 0.5 rho g d^2 Kp + 2 c d sqrt(Kp), Kp = tan^2(45 deg + phi/2). The machine's hydraulics stall at roughly the force
  a 0.5-0.6 m cut produces in sandy gravel; when it stalls the bucket stops part-way along the planned path (completion < 1),
  but channel 1 always shows the WHOLE planned path.
- A cut face of height H and angle beta stands if H <= 4 c sin(beta) cos(phi) / (gamma (1 - cos(beta - phi))) (Culmann);
  otherwise it slumps and the material runs out toward the trench floor.
- Volume: in the teacher, ground lost ~= carried + soil riding on the bucket; nothing is created.

Measured error of this network (held out): RMS 8-11 cm per bite on disturbed cells vs the teacher's own 2.3 cm noise.
Error share: stalled bites 58% (36% of bites stall), cells the bucket cut 42%, cells within 0.5 m of the cut (slumps)
32%, farther cells 26%. A hand-written test showed the peak passive-wedge force along the planned path alone predicts
which bites stall with 91% accuracy and where they stop within 3% of the path (median).

Rules: do not train or fit weights to data with an optimizer, and do not run the network except through the probes
(they run on a PRACTICE set; a separate validation set and two full trenches you never see decide whether your edit is
kept). Prefer small, explainable edits; say what each edit should change, so it can be checked.

checkpoint('orig')
import numpy as np

# ---------------- design constants ----------------
N_cells = 112*80           # padded grid seen by the network
cell_area = 0.05*0.05
V_thr = 1.2                # m^3 planned (signed) cut volume above which the bite is deemed to stall
w_V   = 0.3                # softness (m^3): gate fully open at V_thr + w_V
Vp    = V_thr/(N_cells*cell_area)     # per-cell threshold in "a" units
w_m   = w_V  /(N_cells*cell_area)
g0, O_a, O_s = 20.0, 27.0, 25.0       # e1.0 linear passes
g_d, O_d, g_X, O_X = 20.0, 25.0, 20.0, 45.0   # e1.3 linear passes (d_pre and -d_pre)
g = 40.0                                # gain for rectified/binary signals
g_d1 = 20.0                             # d1.0 depth gain
kappa, Ap = 0.8, 3.0                    # Delta = ReLU(kappa*d - Ap*u)

def zero_group(prefix_conv, prefix_gn, c0, n):
    W[prefix_conv+'.weight'][c0:c0+n] = 0.0
    W[prefix_conv+'.bias'][c0:c0+n] = 0.0
    W[prefix_gn+'.weight'][c0:c0+n] = 0.0
    W[prefix_gn+'.bias'][c0:c0+n] = 0.0

def setup_group(conv, gn, c0, n, K, specs):
    """specs: dict channel -> (gain, offset) for channels whose GN output should be gain*x+offset.
    Channel c0 is the constant K channel (output 0)."""
    zero_group(conv, gn, c0, n)
    W[conv+'.bias'][c0] = K
    sigma0 = K*np.sqrt(n-1)/n
    for c,(gain,off) in specs.items():
        W[gn+'.weight'][c] = gain*sigma0
        W[gn+'.bias'][c]   = gain*K/n + off

# ---------------- e1.0 : inputs -> a (signed volume density), -ch1 -----------------
K=1000.0
setup_group('e1.0','e1.1',32,4,K,{33:(g0,O_a),34:(g0,O_s)})
w=W['e1.0.weight']; b=W['e1.0.bias']
# ch33: a = -ch1 + 0.5*ch2 - Vp
w[33,1,1,1] = -1.0; w[33,2,1,1] = 0.5; b[33] = -Vp
# ch34: s0 = -ch1
w[34,1,1,1] = -1.0
# ch35: -(a+s0)  (zero-sum partner, output 0)
w[35] = -(w[33]+w[34]); b[35] = -(b[33]+b[34])

# ---------------- e1.3 : recover a (for GN-mean broadcast), d_pre=-ch1, -d_pre --------
setup_group('e1.3','e1.4',32,4,K,{34:(g_d,O_d),35:(-g_X,O_X)})
w=W['e1.3.weight']; b=W['e1.3.bias']
w[33,33,1,1] = 1/g0; b[33] = -O_a/g0          # a' (its spatial mean enters the GN mean -> broadcast)
w[34,34,1,1] = 1/g0; b[34] = -O_s/g0          # d_pre = -ch1
w[35] = -w[34]; b[35] = -b[34]                # -d_pre  (zero-sum with d_pre)

# ---------------- e2.0 : P = clamp(50*(d_pre-0.02),0,1) via a,b pair ------------------
setup_group('e2.0','e2.1',64,8,K,{65:(g,0.0),66:(g,0.0)})
w=W['e2.0.weight']; b=W['e2.0.bias']
w[65,34,1,1] = 50/g_d; b[65] = 50*(-O_d/g_d - 0.02)   # a
w[66] = w[65]; b[66] = b[65]-1.0                      # b = a-1
w[67] = -(w[65]+w[66]); b[67] = -(b[65]+b[66])

def and_layer(conv, gn, c0, n, K, out_c, in_pos, in_neg=None, in_gain=g, taps=(1,2)):
    """out_c pre = sum_taps S(x+tap-1) - 1  where S = (y[in_pos]-y[in_neg])/in_gain ; output SiLU(g*pre)"""
    setup_group(conv, gn, c0, n, K, {out_c:(g,0.0)})
    w=W[conv+'.weight']; b=W[conv+'.bias']
    for t in taps:
        w[out_c,in_pos,t,1] += 1/in_gain
        if in_neg is not None: w[out_c,in_neg,t,1] -= 1/in_gain
    b[out_c] = -(len(taps)-1)
    w[out_c+1] = -w[out_c]; b[out_c+1] = -b[out_c]

def pass_layer(conv, gn, c0, n, K, out_c, in_pos, in_gain=g):
    and_layer(conv, gn, c0, n, K, out_c, in_pos, None, in_gain, taps=(1,))

# ---------------- encoder AND chain on P (path continues downstream) -----------------
and_layer('e2.3','e2.4',64,8,K,65,65,66)       # A = P(x) & P(x+1)
and_layer('e3.0','e3.1',128,16,K,129,65)
and_layer('e3.3','e3.4',128,16,K,129,129)
and_layer('e4.0','e4.1',256,32,K,257,129)
and_layer('e4.3','e4.4',256,32,K,257,257)
# ---------------- decoder: pass A down -----------------------------------------------
pass_layer('d3.0','d3.1',128,16,K,129,257)     # up(e4) spare 257
pass_layer('d3.3','d3.4',128,16,K,129,129)
pass_layer('d2.0','d2.1',64,8,K,65,129)        # up(d3) spare 129
pass_layer('d2.3','d2.4',64,8,K,65,65)

# ---------------- d1.0 : u = ReLU(1 - G + A), d = ReLU(d_pre) -------------------------
K1=3000.0
setup_group('d1.0','d1.1',32,4,K1,{33:(g,0.0),34:(g_d1,0.0)})
w=W['d1.0.weight']; b=W['d1.0.bias']
c = 3.0/(2.0*w_m)
# u_pre = 1 + c*[(y106-O_d)/g_d + (y107-O_X)/g_X] + y65/g
w[33,106,1,1] = c/g_d; w[33,107,1,1] = c/g_X; w[33,65,1,1] = 1/g
b[33] = 1.0 - c*(O_d/g_d + O_X/g_X)
# d_pre
w[34,106,1,1] = 1/g_d; b[34] = -O_d/g_d
w[35] = -(w[33]+w[34]); b[35] = -(b[33]+b[34])

# ---------------- d1.3 : P1 = kappa*d - Ap*u  -> ReLU ----------------------------------
setup_group('d1.3','d1.4',32,4,K,{33:(g,0.0)})
w=W['d1.3.weight']; b=W['d1.3.bias']
w[33,34,1,1] = kappa/g_d1; w[33,33,1,1] = -Ap/g
w[34] = -w[33]; b[34] = -b[33]
# ---------------- out -----------------------------------------------------------------
W['out.weight'][0,32:] = 0.0
W['out.weight'][0,33,0,0] = 1/g
print("Vp",Vp,"w_m",w_m,"c",c)
checkpoint('v1')

RESULT: no net edit kept (weights restored to the original). All of my gated-stall side-path variants made the practice error worse, so I rolled them back rather than ship a harmful change.

What I established (probes):
- Drag direction is +x (row index). In stalled bite c143-common-earth_0065 the cut stops at x≈70 of a planned path reaching x≈91; the swept envelope (ch1) is far larger than what the teacher removes (planned signed volume ≈4 m³, exceedance above 0.6 m ≈2.9 m³ vs 0.95 m³ capacity), i.e. the stall/overfill is a global (fill-driven) effect, not a local depth threshold: the deepest part is cut first and the bucket stops in the shallow tail.
- Spare channels are exactly isolated from the original network (all original rows have zero weight on spare inputs; GroupNorm groups are contiguous), so a side path can be built without touching the original function.

What I built (spare channels only, derived analytically, no fitting):
1. "K-trick" to pass signals through GroupNorm deterministically: one spare channel carries a large constant K (conv bias), the other channels are made zero-sum, so the group mean/std are known and the affine (γ=g·σ0, β=gK/n+offset) yields output = g·x + offset (verified by an e1 feature probe to ~1%).
2. A global flag through the GroupNorm mean: an un-paired channel whose spatial mean is (planned cut volume − prior volume)/area shifts the whole spare group by a known amount; two channels with opposite gains recover that global scalar in d1.0. This classifier did separate stalled from completed practice bites perfectly (completed-bite error stayed bit-identical at 0.1077 while the gate acted only on stalled bites).
3. A causal AND chain on the "bucket below ground" indicator (taps x, x+1, through e2–e4, passed down d3–d2) meant to flag the last ~1 m of the active path, and in d1.3 a ReLU-multiplication Δ = ReLU(κ·amp − 3·ReLU(1−G+40A)) added to the residual via out.weight[0,33].

Outcome: with amplitude = depth (v4) or = −prior (v5) the stalled-bite RMS went from 0.133 to 0.745 m (completed unchanged). The gate opened over the whole planned path on stalled bites (the AND-chain term did not close it), and cancelling the prior/depth there revealed that on the practice set the original residual already offsets the prior beyond the stall, so suppression adds error. With no forward budget left to locate the chain fault, I restored the original weights. Expected change in stalled-bite error from the submitted state: 0 (network identical to the original).
